title: A verdict must be a check the machine can run
goal: Verdicts are prose today, so they lie in both directions: the roadmap carried 13 false DELIVERED claims whose components exist but that no production path reaches, and in one hour I produced three confidently wrong refutations (77 phantom candidates from test names and module declarations, then a nextest filter artifact, then prose read as tests). Every one of those errors came from a grep that counted the wrong thing. The fix is to make each verdict carry the command that establishes it: check-reachability.py decides delivered vs refuted by production call sites of a distinctive symbol, stripping comments, strings, module declarations and #[cfg(test)] blocks so that only real code counts, and refusing common words that produce hundreds of meaningless hits. check-roadmap-verdict.py runs a verdict's declared check and requires it to pass, and audits existing delivered verdicts for reachability.
